When the processes that bear the demands split or merge, that correspondence may not be a bijection, and [CLAIM-287](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-287.md) says the continuity it would follow can branch and is not an identity relation. | [QUESTION-124](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-124.md) | When do endorsement dynamics turn a transient conflict among an organization's demands into a persistent regime of frustration, and can the condition be stated in an architecture-sensitive update geometry such as modular duality's? | A33's proposed next result, U33 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, after the owner asked whether "the modular duality program might be useful to us here": "characterize frustration in a modular update geometry, then ask when the dynamics of endorsement convert a temporary optimization conflict into a persistent organizational regime." The record has the static parts, the residual and its certificate ([CLAIM-365](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-365.md)) and the structural/governance split ([CLAIM-357](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-357.md)), and a linear capture threshold ([CLAIM-330](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-330.md)). It has no dynamics joining them. An answer gives a condition on the coupling of endorsement to demands under which governance-induced frustration persists after the conflict that started it is gone, and says whether the update geometry enters it. | Open |
| [QUESTION-125](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-125.md) | When a candidate block gains or loses the gap that isolates it as a parameter varies, does the change in its identifiable boundary coincide with a bifurcation of its dynamics, and what does each way of their coming apart show? | A6 §2 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, which the owner took up with "flesh this out further". The record identifies a unit by a gap in its interaction structure ([CLAIM-157](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-157.md), [CLAIM-164](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-164.md)) and finds regime changes by stability ([CLAIM-330](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-330.md)). Both are spectral facts about a parameter-dependent system, but they are different facts, and nothing in the record pairs them. A6: "Their divergence may be just as revealing as their coincidence." An answer is a construction or a system in which the two transitions coincide, one in which the regime changes with the block unchanged, and one in which the block changes with the behaviour unchanged, with what each shows about regime, individual and function. | Open |
| [QUESTION-126](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-126.md) | Does an organization's actual allocation of authority track the demands that bind its feasible adaptation, or does it systematically privilege something else? | A35 §3.2 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, worded there: "Does the organization's actual allocation of authority track the demands that constrain its feasible adaptation, or does it systematically privilege something else?" The dual of the frustration residual ([CLAIM-365](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-365.md)) picks out, by its multipliers λ, the combination of demands that binds; the operator model's weights w are the influence governance actually grants ([TERM-053](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-053.md)). A35: "these dual multipliers are not endorsement weights." An answer measures both in one organization and says whether w follows λ, and if not what it follows instead. | Open |
| [QUESTION-131](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-131.md) | How does structural frustration among jointly incompatible demands relate to operative thwarting of a constituent's demands, and under what conditions can one occur without the other? | Raised in the reviews the owner relayed on 2026-10-18, after the filing of the exchange of 2026-10-17. Structural frustration has a settled formal definition: a collection of demands is structurally frustrated when no outcome attainable under the specified constraints meets them all, S ∉ 𝒦(𝒪; D) ([CLAIM-347](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-347.md)). What is open is how it relates to operative thwarting, where a particular constituent's live demand is counteracted by an identifiable constraint or countervailing process. Physics frustration ([CLAIM-153](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-153.md)) is the structural sense, and self-determination theory's need thwarting ([THEORY-052](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-052.md)) the operative one. An answer says when structural incompatibility shows up as thwarting, whether thwarting can occur where joint satisfaction is possible, and what evidence attributes either to a bearer. Merely failing to realize an attainable set of requirements is neither. | Open |
| [QUESTION-132](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-132.md) | Under what conditions do initially equivalent adaptive operators differentiate into functionally complementary specialists that each have positive recovery growth when rare, rather than into roles kept in place by external load balancing or by persistent authority asymmetries? | The central mathematical question of the synthesis the owner relayed on 2026-10-18. [QUESTION-083](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-083.md) asks whether operators sharing one update rule can come to hold differentiated authority. This asks the coexistence version: does the differentiation produce stabilizing negative frequency dependence, meaning every specialist recovers when rare (Chesson's stabilizing mechanisms, [LIT-1219](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1219.md), unread)? Or is it held in place from outside, or by one process's entrenched advantage? An answer is a population model that derives the interaction structure from learned contributions, states recovery criteria, and finds the regimes of coexistence and exclusion. Heterogeneous embeddings, unequal routing weights or persistent expert identities do not answer it. | Open |
| [QUESTION-133](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-133.md) | Can a population of operators whose demands are jointly infeasible under one functional organization develop a differentiated or compositional repertoire that makes them jointly feasible, without suppressing, weakening or deleting any of those demands? | From the synthesis the owner relayed on 2026-10-18, which called it the most conceptually interesting new connection. [CLAIM-347](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-347.md) defines structural frustration as joint infeasibility and relief as enlargement of the compatibility complex under fixed demands. [CASE-119](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-119.md) shows relief by enlarging the attainable set, with every pair compatible and the triple not, until a composite policy appears. The question is whether learning, specialization or recomposition can bring this about endogenously. An answer is a model that keeps the acceptance sets fixed while learning changes what is attainable and strictly enlarges the complex. Apparent relief that comes only from removing a demand or redefining success does not count. | Open |
| [QUESTION-134](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-134.md) | When influence decides access to learning opportunities, does the resulting feedback make a marginalized specialist lose its competence, so that it cannot recover influence even when its former niche becomes relevant again? | From the synthesis the owner relayed on 2026-10-18. [CLAIM-277](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-277.md)'s note of 2026-10-18 records niche exclusion by authority deprivation: low exposure, poor competence estimates, low endorsement, lower exposure. This asks whether the loop goes further and destroys the competence, not just the measurement of it. When training opportunities follow influence, a specialist denied opportunities may become genuinely unable to do its job. An answer separates loss of influence, loss of competence and loss of access to evaluation. That gives an operational test for one mechanism of domination without defining domination as holding less authority. | Open |
| [QUESTION-135](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-135.md) | When does spectral differentiation among learned features correspond to stabilizing coexistence among the processes that implement them, and what besides the feature geometry decides it? | From the synthesis the owner relayed on 2026-10-18. In symmetric resource-mediated competition the interaction matrix is the Gram matrix of the components' feature vectors, A = UᵀU, so representational redundancy and competitive overlap are one object ([CLAIM-369](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-369.md)). In the two-component case invasion growth equals λ_min(A) ([CASE-118](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-118.md)). But the same A supports coexistence or exclusion depending on the growth rates. An answer says when the Gram spectrum of a learned representation predicts that the processes carrying its features will coexist, and what else, such as supply, task distribution or evaluation opportunities, has to be fixed for it to. | Open |
| [QUESTION-147](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-147.md) | In a second system of near-identical units on a known graph, are the synchronized clusters the symmetry orbits computed in advance, and does each cluster desynchronize in isolation where its own transverse block predicts? | The empirical condition formerly in [THEORY-276](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-276.md)'s promote_when. On 2026-10-19 [THEORY-276](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-276.md) was promoted: that symmetry orbits are flow-invariant synchronization clusters, and that a cluster whose own factor moves nothing else can desynchronize while the others stay synchronized, was checked by a fixed-point-subspace derivation. Whether the stability predictions hold up in a second physical or biological system, as the record's use of this result as a coupling signature ([QUESTION-063](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-063.md)) needs, rests on one 11-node experiment. | Open |
| [QUESTION-151](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-151.md) | Does the decoupling of reproducibility from convergence survive a consensus with memory, where a challenger must win repeatedly or evidence accumulates, and scientists can learn? | The promotion condition formerly on [THEORY-295](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-295.md), moved here when [THEORY-295](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-295.md) was narrowed to a consensus that a single test can replace and promoted on 2026-10-19 ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v3). [LIT-988](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-988.md) shows the decoupling only for a memoryless consensus and agents that do not learn. Whether a population that never pits the true model against the consensus still holds a reproducible false consensus once the consensus has memory is untested. | Open |
| [QUESTION-152](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-152.md) | Does the impossibility of robustly rational proposition-wise aggregation extend from categorical judgments to corporate attitudes in general: degrees of belief, desires, intentions or emotions? | The second clause of [THEORY-127](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-127.md)'s former promote_when. On 2026-10-19 [THEORY-127](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-127.md) was promoted, narrowed, after the record re-derived Proposition 3 of List and Pettit (2006) for categorical judgments. List (2014), [LIT-700](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-700.md), makes holistic supervenience the mark of corporate attitudes in general. Neither paper proves the impossibility for attitudes other than binary judgments, and the record holds no such result. | Open |
| [QUESTION-154](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-154.md) | Does a block coarse-graining that maximizes the information its coarse variables keep about the far environment, but falls short of full capture with their number and type fixed, keep the renormalized Hamiltonian's longer-range couplings bounded by the information lost, in two or more dimensions? | The promotion condition formerly on [THEORY-198](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-198.md), moved here unchanged when [THEORY-198](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-198.md) was narrowed and promoted on 2026-10-19. The perfect case is proved: full capture makes the coarse measure factorize across the block. The maximizers actually found fall short of full capture, and for them the link to a short-ranged Hamiltonian is shown only on 1D chains. | Open |
| [QUESTION-169](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-169.md) | On a contested shared canvas, do lasting artworks as a population receive sustained overwrites and repairs, and does adding interaction features make coalition survival predictable early? | The promotion condition formerly on [THEORY-216](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-216.md), moved here when [THEORY-216](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-216.md) was narrowed to what Wu and Silva measured on the 2017 r/place log and promoted on 2026-10-19 ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v3). [LIT-1032](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1032.md) shows persistence under attack in ten illustrated lifecycles and low early predictability from four coalition-state features. How common the first is, and whether the second is in the dynamics or in the feature set, are untested. | Open |
| [QUESTION-170](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-170.md) | When no single setting of a regulator is stable in every environment it may meet, must any system that comes to keep its essential variables within limits carry a channel from those variables to the parameters of its regulation, whether or not it adapts by trial and error? | Filed when the promotion audit (batch 032, [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v2) narrowed and promoted [THEORY-324](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-324.md). Ashby's necessity was re-derived for systems that follow the trial-and-error rule, where it is close to definitional. The former promote_when asked it of any system that comes to keep its essential variables within limits, which is wider. This question holds that wider form. | Open |
| [QUESTION-173](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-173.md) | Does the free-riding structure of truth-and-obstinacy debate survive with more than two debaters or with strategies richer than fixed, memoryless premise and conclusion rules? | The promotion condition formerly on [THEORY-290](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-290.md), moved here when [THEORY-290](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-290.md) was narrowed to the two-debater, three-proposition model it was computed in and promoted on 2026-10-19 ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v3). [LIT-966](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-966.md) finds that debaters who value true belief but pay to revise free-ride on one another's bold arguments, in a model with two players and fixed, memoryless strategies. Whether the structure holds for groups, or for debaters who can target a partner's false beliefs, is not shown. | Open |
